name: Post-Interpolative Importance Function
definition: An importance function that maps points in the volume to $n$ distinct values in [0,1], creating a step function along a ray. This eliminates the need for smoothing discontinuities from discretized importance and preserves fine details better than pre-interpolative classification.
summary: The Post-Interpolative Importance Function is a visibility optimization technique that maps interpolated volume data to discrete step functions, preserving fine details lost by pre-interpolative smoothing.
